pairs.subject: prompt-safety
pairs.evidence: lib/analysis/kg-verdict.ts:268 The KG verdict gate checks model-emitted identifiers against the store only when the caller supplies knownIds. If the caller omits it, edge endpoints and prose-cited urns are not resolved at all, and the result still comes back as an unqualified ok:true. The same opt-in shape is in verdict.ts:209 and law-verdict.ts:247-248, so the 'every identifier is validated against the live store' rule is conditional, not unconditional.

techniques.evidence: lib/analysis/kg-verdict.ts:303 The closed grammar is real: additionalProperties:false, enum rel/kind, checkExactKeys. But an edge endpoint passes when the same model output declared it as a node. The anti-hallucination sweep (ENTITY_URN, line 98) matches only psp:* urns, so a self-declared fabricated id such as company:ico:… passes as an endpoint without any existence check against the store. The whole check is also skipped when knownIds is absent.

lib/analysis/verdict.ts:209 When no id set is supplied, the entity-membership check silently does not run, and ValidationResult has no field recording that it was not inspected. A skipped check and a passed check produce the same ok:true.

lib/analysis/law-verdict.ts:13 The consequential output of the law forensic channel is bounded: gated findings are stored pending_review for a human, and verdict-provenance.ts discloses a 'machine' rung to readers. Persuasive prose channels are not separately assigned a payoff.

lib/analysis/law-verdict.ts:257 Model-authored web/bill_text citation sources are allowlisted to http(s) schemes before persist, and LAW_PIPELINE_JARGON rejects cache file paths in prose. Secret masking and markup neutralization are not in this context; the models here are not shown credentials.
lib/analysis/language-gate.ts:14 The persist-time and render-time gates are one TypeScript module imported at both ends, so there is no second runtime and no mirrored implementation to drift.

lib/analysis/tripwires.ts:1 These 'tripwires' are deterministic graph-invariant candidate generators, not prompt canaries. The context assembles no prompt, so it plants no canary or nonce, and the validators do not screen output for one.

pairs.registryProposal: model-output-as-untrusted could name a specific hole: the 'declared in the same output' escape hatch. A validator that accepts identifiers the model introduced elsewhere in the same response as valid references turns the existence check into self-attestation. The technique should say that model-declared new entities need their own existence/kind gate, and must not become trusted endpoints for other operations in the same response.
